stemMd: A right triangle has an acute angle of 30° and hypotenuse 14 cm. What is the side opposite the 30° angle?
explanationMd: The opposite side equals hypotenuse times sine of the angle. Since sin30°=1/2, its length is 14×1/2=7 cm. In a thirty-sixty-ninety triangle, the shorter leg is half the hypotenuse.

distractorRationale.b: An opposite leg cannot exceed the hypotenuse here.
distractorRationale.d: This uses a tangent-related ratio instead of sine of thirty degrees.
